clue.text: Kills deer with wickedness

parts.note: a doe is a female deer
sin is wrongdoing or wickedness

explanation.surface: Someone slaughters deer out of sheer malice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deer' looks plural, but here it gives a single female deer; the word break then falls after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone in is slang for murdering them.

clue.text: Large slice rising to entrance householder

explanation.surface: A big slice of something being lifted up to a homeowner's front door.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick-cut slab of bread is a British colloquial sense; the other is the raised step leading up to a householder's front entrance.

clue.text: Detested having river boxed in

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, a crossword favourite
crated means packed into a box

explanation.surface: Someone hated being penned in by a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to loathe or curse, so execrated is a synonym of hated.

clue.text: Little mischief's done by individual members

parts.note: I is the single individual, the first person
MPs are Members of Parliament

explanation.surface: Small pranks carried out by particular members of a group.
explanation.definitionFit: Small sprites or naughty children are the ones who do petty mischief.

clue.text: Silly' things to. have with cheese

explanation.surface: Daft biscuits to eat with a cheese course.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray apostrophe and full stop are print specks in the scanned clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Crazy, in British slang; also the plain dry biscuits served with a cheeseboard.

clue.text: Cracksman @draws lots

explanation.surface: A safebreaker picks names out of a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: A J Raffles is E W Hornung's fictional gentleman safebreaker; the '@' is a print speck.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffles is the famous fictional burglar; as a verb it means holds a lottery for prizes.

clue.text: Just miss a place to emerge we hear

indicators.note: signals that the words are matched by their spoken sound, not spelling

parts.note: to come forth is to emerge

explanation.surface: Someone narrowly misses a podium place as they come out.
explanation.walkthrough: FORTH and FOURTH sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Finishing in fourth position just misses out on the medals in a race.

clue.text: Something on the bill is super in Hollywood

explanation.surface: A surcharge appears on the tab for a superb Hollywood film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Super' is short for supernumerary, a non-speaking walk-on actor.
explanation.definitionFit: An added charge on a bill; and a crowd-scene film actor, also called a super.

clue.text: Transfix southern king going to jug

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
a ewer is a large water jug

explanation.surface: A southern monarch heading off to prison is impaled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jug' looks like prison slang but is just a pitcher.
explanation.definitionFit: To skewer something is to pierce it through, as with a spit.

clue.text: Proposal for change of place

explanation.surface: A suggestion that we relocate.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal suggestion put to a meeting; and movement from one position to another.

clue.text: Finished demonstration with more alcohol than usual

parts.note: over means ended or finished
a proof is a demonstration that something is true

explanation.surface: Someone completes a demonstration involving strong drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits stronger than the standard proof strength are described this way.

clue.text: Joint going to prelate's head

explanation.surface: A joint is passed to the bishop's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpentry corner joint cut at an angle; also the tall headdress a bishop wears.

clue.text: Island coming under Jersey

explanation.surface: A Channel Island ranked below Jersey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jersey' suggests the Channel Island but is the knitted garment: a sark is a Scots word for a shirt, worn under it.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the small Channel Islands; and a shirt, worn beneath a sweater.

clue.text: Cab driver's account of menu

explanation.surface: A taxi driver's tally of the dishes on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: A cabbie's passenger is a fare, so a cab driver's account is the bill for that fare.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant's list of dishes; read literally, the invoice for a taxi ride.

clue.text: Object of time and motion study is to prevent a Socialist collapse

definitions.text: Object of time and motion study

explanation.surface: An efficiency study is meant to stop the left-wing party falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is Britain's socialist party; to save it is to stop it collapsing.
explanation.definitionFit: Efficiency studies aim to cut workers' effort; and rescuing the Labour Party from ruin.

clue.text: Get on at Waterloo from two different quarters by coach

parts.note: east, one compass quarter, is E
north, another compass quarter, is N
to coach is to train

explanation.surface: Boarding at a London station from two directions on a bus.
explanation.walkthrough: Waterloo is a major London railway terminus; 'coach' is the verb, not a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrain is to board a railway carriage, as at a station.

clue.text: Discontented go to church in spring

parts.note: sour means grumpy or discontented
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The disgruntled attend church in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' is not the season but a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring is where a river or stream rises, its origin.

clue.text: Kind of competition offering a razor

explanation.surface: A contest that comes with a shaving blade.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruthless, merciless rivalry is so described; and an open straight-blade razor bears the name.

clue.text: Revenge for a rare slip maybe

indicators.note: suggests the letters of these words may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Getting your own back for an uncommon mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' shuffles RARE SLIP into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A retaliatory act is a form of vengeance.

clue.text: Coming with a daughter to opening

parts.note: D abbreviates daughter in genealogy
a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: Someone arrives with a daughter for a première.
explanation.definitionFit: An advent is an arrival, especially of something important.

clue.text: It can be a great draw to the western railway

definitions.text: It can be a great draw

parts.note: W abbreviates western
a line is a railway track

explanation.surface: Something hugely popular, rather like the Great Western Railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'great draw' sounds like a crowd-puller, but means a big pull: a rope for towing. The Great Western was a famous British railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A tow rope pulls a vehicle or boat, so it does the drawing.

clue.text: Style adopted by Cockney female with nobility

parts.note: a Cockney drops the H, so a hen, a female bird, is 'en
a title is a rank of nobility

explanation.surface: A fashion taken up by an East End woman with aristocratic airs.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the London East End accent, which drops initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: To style someone is to give them a name or designation.

clue.text: Adorn a nicer variation with hydrogen

indicators.note: a variation of a word changes the order of its letters

parts.note: H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: Decorate a more pleasant version using a gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variation' turns NICER into ENRIC.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrich can mean to embellish or decorate.

clue.text: Rascal one gave sea food

parts.note: a scamp is a rascal
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A rogue handed out some fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaded langoustine tails are a popular seafood dish.

clue.text: Occasional customer protected child in workhouse

parts.note: a casual is an occasional, irregular visitor
a ward is a child under a guardian's protection

explanation.surface: An irregular visitor shields a child in the poorhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Workhouses were Victorian British poorhouses; their casual ward housed passing vagrants overnight.
explanation.definitionFit: The section for overnight vagrants was a department found within a workhouse.

clue.text: Dawn of the Students' Union literally

parts.note: the letters N U S, initials of the National Union of Students, are what you see when a three-letter star word is written going upward in a down light

explanation.surface: The beginning of student politics.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: 'literally' says to take the answer as an instruction, 'write SUN going up', which in a down entry shows NUS, the National Union of Students.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunrise is the moment of daybreak.

clue.text: Cleaner burn

explanation.surface: A domestic help gets scorched.
explanation.definitionFit: A charwoman is a British word for a cleaning lady; also to scorch or blacken.

clue.text: Cheese is endlessly short

indicators.note: without an end, so the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: brief means short

explanation.surface: A cheese is always in short supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the last letter from BRIEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft French cheese.

clue.text: Fruit to give a chap some zip

parts.note: a chap is a man
zip is energy or go

explanation.surface: Eating fruit to put some pep into a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical stone fruit.

clue.text: Not wanting to know how to saddle oneself with debts

parts.note: to incur is to bring a burden on oneself
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: Lacking interest in how one ends up loaded with debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking curiosity has no wish to find things out.

clue.text: Told confession of person just divorced

explanation.surface: Someone tells how they just split from their spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads as 'I'm parted', what a newly divorced person might say.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart news is to tell it; split as a statement, it is a newly separated person admitting they have split up.

clue.text: Valet's strangely chaste

indicators.note: signals that the letters are put in an odd new order

parts.note: the word valet with its S included as a letter

explanation.surface: A manservant is unexpectedly pure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges VALETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Vestal virgins were Roman priestesses sworn to celibacy, so the word means pure.
